mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such tightening episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes, or the average return exceeds +1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of such triggers, or the median return is not statistically negative at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) and a decline in the housing starts index (HOUST) by more than 5% month-over-month indicates a sectoral shift away from construction toward manufacturing, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to real sector rotation.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of such co-movement episodes, or the average return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) rises above 4% while the federal funds rate is below 2%, it signals a delayed policy response to inflation, which increases uncertainty and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 45% of such regimes, or the median return is not statistically negative.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) above trend by more than 3% for three consecutive months signals robust consumer demand, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > +3% above trend for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of such episodes, or the average return is not statistically positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals accelerating labor market absorption, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate hiring, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such triggers, or the median return is not statistically positive.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 2% month-over-month indicates a broad-based contraction in the manufacturing and construction sectors, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of monetary policy stance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes, or the median return is not statistically negative.
